The goal of this lab is to become familiar with processing canopy height products from *full name here* (GEDI) and National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) to understand how and why these products may differ and how they can be used in ecological applications. Analysis will be done for a single year, 2022, at one NEON site, Harvard forest, in the Northeastern United States. *insert short description about Harvard forest vegetation, etc, here*

# Setup

## install packages

Install Packages 
```{r}
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse",
  "sf",            # vector data (flight boxes, GEDI points, footprint buffers)
  "terra",         # rasters (NEON CHM tiles, mosaicking, extraction)
  "neonUtilities", # downloading NEON AOP data
  "dplyr",         # filtering/summarizing tables
  "ggplot2",       # plots
  "lubridate",     # pulling year/month from GEDI dates (for leaf-on filtering)
  "arrow",         # reading Parquet files (chewie caches GEDI this way)
  "remotes",        # for installing chewie from GitHub
  "exactextractr", 
  "maps", 
  "mapview",
  "ggpubr",
  "patchwork"))

```

Load Library
```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(terra)
library(neonUtilities)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(arrow)
library(remotes)
library(exactextractr)
library(maps)
library(mapview)
library(ggpubr)
library(patchwork)

```


# Part A: Get GEDI flyovers at Harvard forest

## NEON AOP flight boxes

NEON has pre made AOP flight boundaries for all sites. See more [here](https://www.neonscience.org/data-collection/flight-box-design).

```{r}
# read in all flight boxes from project directory 
aop <- st_read("AOP_flightBoxes/AOP_flightboxesAllSites.shp")

# view/explore
aop
names(aop)
aop[[3]] # shows site names [[4]] for site ID
st_crs(aop) # retrieve coordinate reference system 

# plot 
# US state outlines as an sf object
states <- st_as_sf(maps::map("state", plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE))

# flight boxes are tiny at national scale, so plot their centroids as points
aop_pts <- aop |>
  st_transform(5070) |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_centroid()

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = "grey95", color = "grey60") +
  geom_sf(data = aop_pts, color = "darkgreen", size = 1.5) +
  coord_sf(crs = st_crs(5070)) +   # USA Contiguous Albers Equal Area
  labs(title = "NEON AOP flight boxes") +
  theme_minimal()


```

## Pull out Harvard Forest from NEON AOP's

```{r}
harv <- aop[aop$siteID == "HARV",]

# view 
view(harv) # should only have rows for Harvard forest/watershed 

# keep only priority 1 - priority differentiates how often the area gets flown over/has images taken 
harv_p1 <- harv |> 
  filter(priority == 1)

# plot both
mapview(harv, col.regions = "grey",
        map.types = c("Esri.WorldImagery", "OpenStreetMap", "CartoDB.Positron")) +
  mapview(harv_p1, col.regions = "red") # red is the P1 boundary we use 
```

## RESTART HERE - filter GEDI data

```{r}
# read in clipped gedi data 
harv_gedi <- st_read("lab_data/gedi_data.gpkg")

# filtering process
step0 <- harv_gedi
step1 <- step0 |> filter(quality_flag == 1) # GEDI's overall quality flag - removes clouds
step2 <- step1 |> filter(degrade_flag == 0) # no instrument/pointing problems
step3 <- step2 |> filter(sensitivity >= 0.95) # beam could see through the canopy to the ground
step4 <- step3 |> filter(leaf_off_flag == 0)           # leaf-on conditions

# see how many shots remain after each filtering step
data.frame(
  step = c("all shots", "quality_flag", "degrade_flag", "sensitivity", "leaf-on"),
  n    = c(nrow(step0), nrow(step1), nrow(step2), nrow(step3), nrow(step4))
) # should be left with ~1300 shots at step 5

# rewrite data frame with new quality control 
harv_gedi_qc <- step4

# save cleaned data 
 st_write(harv_gedi_qc, "lab_data/lab_gedi_qc.gpkg", delete_dsn = TRUE)

# map 
removed <- step0[!step0$shot_number %in% harv_gedi_qc$shot_number, ]

mapview(harv_p1, col.regions = "red", alpha.regions = 0.1,
        map.types = c("Esri.WorldImagery", "OpenStreetMap")) +
  mapview(removed, col.regions = "grey", cex = 1.5, lwd = 0, layer.name = "Removed shots") +
  mapview(harv_gedi_qc, zcol = "rh98", cex = 2, lwd = 0, layer.name = "Kept shots (RH98, m)")

```

# Part B - Explore NEON data

## SKIP FOR LAB - Figure out which years have AOPs from NEON.

Data is too large to be downloaded during class (also need a free NEON account). Look [here](https://data.neonscience.org/data-products/DP3.30015.001) to learn more about downloading NEON ecosystem structure data.

```{r}
chm_dir <- "Data/Neon_data/NEON.D01.HARV.DP3.30015.001.2022-08.basic.20261101T221639Z.RELEASE-2026"      # Set wd to where filds are

tifs <- list.files(chm_dir, pattern = "CHM\\.tif$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE) # List files
tif_year <- sub(".*DP3\\.30015\\.001\\.(\\d{4})-\\d{2}.*", "\\1", tifs)
table(tif_year)

tifs_2022 <- tifs[tif_year == "2022"]   # keep only 2022 tiles                           # Filter by year

```

## SKIP FOR LAB - Match NEON with GEDI data by location

```{r}
# read in GEDI data and keep 2019 shots to match the NEON flight year
harv_gedi <- st_read("lab_data/lab_gedi_qc.gpkg")

# stitch the 2022 tiles into one virtual raster
chm_2022 <- vrt(tifs_2022)
#
crs(chm_2022)                          # crs "ESPG 32618"
crs(harv_p1)                           # crs "EPSG 4326"

# Not the same coordinate system

# transform GEDI data to the right format to be matched with NEON
gedi_fp <- harv_gedi |>
  st_transform(crs(chm_2022)) |> # transform to same coordinate system as NEON
  st_buffer(12.5)                # 25 m circle around each GEDI point
```

## RESTART HERE - join files by shot number

***neon_chm_at_gedi_2022.csv has 2019, 2022, 2024*** added filter in code chunk 

```{r}
harv_gedi   <- st_read("lab_data/lab_gedi_qc.gpkg")
chm_results <- read.csv("lab_data/neon_chm_at_gedi_2022.csv",
                        colClasses = c(shot_number = "character"))

gedi_neon <- harv_gedi |>
  mutate(shot_number = as.character(shot_number)) |>
  inner_join(chm_results, by = "shot_number") |> 
  rename(GEDI_rh98 = rh98, NEON_rh98 = chm_p98) |>
  relocate(shot_number, GEDI_rh98, NEON_rh98)

nrow(gedi_neon)   # footprints with both a GEDI and a NEON height

st_write(gedi_neon, "lab_data/gedi_neon_2022.gpkg", delete_dsn = TRUE) # final dataset
```

# Part C - Plots and Analysis

First view the selected GEDI shots within the NEON AOP

Then Plot GEDI vs NEON height (98) metrics against eachother, examine rmse and bias 

Then look at difference between the two products at each site
```{r}

# Plot the matched locations 
mapview(harv_p1, col.regions = "red", alpha.regions = 0.1,
        map.types = c("Esri.WorldImagery", "OpenStreetMap")) +
  mapview(gedi_neon, zcol = "GEDI_rh98", cex = 4, lwd = 0,
          label = gedi_neon$Site_id,
          layer.name = "GEDI shots with NEON (RH98, m)")

gedi_neon_nogeom <- st_drop_geometry(gedi_neon)

ggplot(gedi_neon_nogeom, aes(x = GEDI_rh98, y = NEON_rh98)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_point(aes(color = Site_id), size = 5, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_cor(aes(label = paste(after_stat(r.label), after_stat(rr.label), sep = "~`,`~")),
           label.x.npc = "left", label.y.npc = "top") +
  labs(x = "GEDI rh98 (m)", y = "NEON CHM rh98 (m)", color = "Site ID") +
  theme_bw()

rmse <- sqrt(mean((gedi_neon_nogeom$GEDI_rh98 - gedi_neon_nogeom$NEON_rh98)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
bias <- mean(gedi_neon_nogeom$GEDI_rh98 - gedi_neon_nogeom$NEON_rh98, na.rm = TRUE)

rmse
bias

gedi_neon_nogeom %>% 
  group_by(Site_id) %>% 
  mutate(diff = GEDI_rh98 - NEON_rh98) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Site_id, y = diff, color = Site_id)) +
  geom_point(size = 5, alpha = 0.8)+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Site ID", y = "GEDI − NEON rh98 (m)", color = "Site ID") +
  theme_bw()

```

Comparing GEDI and NEON resolutions 

GEDI products are 25 m resolution circles while NEON is 1m resolution given as a 1km tile. 

GEDI has one value assigned to the circle while NEON has many more pixels each with their own value. Below is looking at the differences and visualizing why it may matter. 
```{r}

# GEDI histogram 
p_gedi <- ggplot() +
  geom_col(aes(x = gedi_row$GEDI_rh98, y = 1), width = 1, fill = "red", alpha = 0.8) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0,30)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:1, limits = c(0, 1.1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "GEDI shots (n)") +
  theme_bw()

# Neon histogram
p_neon <- ggplot(px_a, aes(chm, weight = coverage_fraction)) +   # Because neon pixels often are at GEDI boundary edge, use weight to give meaning to that value
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "grey70", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = gedi_row$NEON_rh98, color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0,30)) +
  labs(x = "Height (m)", y = "NEON pixels (coverage-weighted)") +
  theme_bw()

p_hists <- p_gedi / p_neon + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 3))

p_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = neon_raster_df, aes(x, y, fill = chm)) +
  geom_sf(data = fp_a, fill = NA, color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = gedi_pt, color = "red", size = 2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "CHM (m)", option = "viridis") +
  coord_sf(crs = st_crs(fp_a)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()

p_map | p_hists + plot_annotation(title = "Site A GEDI vs NEON")

# if not working output image is saved in "lab_outputs" as gedi_site_A_comparison.png

```
